utterances.text: Before that day, had you tried to deliver bread to your parents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said that there was light in the sky, the visibility was good. Do you remember how long it was after the first light in the sky that you were wounded, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: No, I couldn't tell you exactly. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On previous occasions when you had taken bread to your parents, had you done so at a particular time of day or night, or in particular conditions, or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Only during the night. Only when it was dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any reason for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Since the shooting was almost constant in that area, we were forced to move around by night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September of last year, did you revisit the place where you were wounded, that is, September 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in the company of an investigator and some other people from the Prosecutor's office at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us where it was on your body that you were wounded.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: The left upper arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you said that you were on the road itself at the time. Were you walking or standing or running, or what, at the time that you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: When I was wounded, I was walking and pushing a trolley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it by what you have said that you were pushing the trolley in front of you. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: No. The trolley was behind me and I was pulling it with my right hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened, if anything, shortly before you were shot? Did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I heard a shot, a burst of gunfire. Two or three bullets were fired before I was hit myself. The bullets whizzed past me or whizzed up above my head and went past me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you indicated earlier that you were shot on your arm, your left arm. Could you indicate more precisely where it was that you -- that the bullet entered your body, by pointing to the relevant part of your body.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes. The bullet entered here and exited there, behind. Went in here, came out there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean that the bullet entered on the outer part of your left upper arm and exited on the inner side of your left upper arm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes. It went in through the front and exited through the back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I automatically tried to take shelter, take cover, and I went into a canal, waited for the situation to calm down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: I stayed there until a car went by, came by, and the driver of that car took me to my parents' place, who were some 200 metres away. They lived 200 metres away from the spot where the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, for what period of time were you in that canal, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: About ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you later taken to receive medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes. Not long afterwards, the same driver returned to fetch me, and he took me to the infirmary, where I was given first aid and an anti-tetanus shot, and then I went to Kosevo Hospital after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I notice we have about five minutes left. I think that would be sufficient time to show the video, if that's convenient to the Trial Chamber, the video for this particular incident. It's a redacted video. I think it only runs for about three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be shown a video with the following exhibit number: P3280B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst that is being prepared, sir, would you please look at the computer screen in front of you, and I think the Chamber usher will allow you to view a video on it, which will shortly be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. L, you'll be shown the video now. We'll stop soon afterwards. So would you please concentrate very much, because tomorrow we'll continue. And if necessary, of course, it could be replayed to you if you have any doubt on whether it's still in your memory. But you can look at it first now. Yes. [Videotape played]: INVESTIGATOR: Please stand where you were standing to the best of your recollection when you were shot. I will now mark that spot in yellow paint with a figure "X." Please assume the position at the spot you indicated, the position you were in, to the best of your recollection, at the time you were shot. Please point in the general direction from which you heard gunfire at the time you were shot, to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Ierace. Do you intend to put any questions, or shall we stop here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just a few questions, Mr. President, if that's convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One or two, but I said 10 to 15 minutes. We are close to 15 minutes, so please proceed but keep in mind the clock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although your face was not visible in that video, did you nevertheless recognise the situation and yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The investigator asked you to do certain things. In carrying out his directions, did you do them truthfully and to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS L
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further this afternoon, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ierace. Mr. L, it was only a very short this afternoon. But for practical reasons we have to stop now, and we'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. Our apologies for just being called for such a short period of time. But as I said, tomorrow we'll continue. We'll then adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, in this same courtroom.
